title: Volatility forecast comparison using imperfect volatility proxies
one_line_what_it_does: Necessary-and-sufficient characterisation of loss functions robust to proxy noise (Bregman-type) and (Prop 3-4) of the robust AND homogeneous subfamily; b=-1 member is h - s2 + s2 log(s2/h), i.e. the Poisson/KL deviance, b=-2 is QLIKE (degree 0); homogeneous loss => ranking invariant to constant rescaling of data
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Thm 3 (Patton-2011-style N&S condition with homogeneity; the Poisson/KL deviance is already a named member, degree 1 not 0); Prop 2 (rescaling of proxy / ranking depends on units); finance analogue

title: Order-sensitivity and equivariance of scoring functions
one_line_what_it_does: Defines and characterises scoring functions with positively homogeneous score differences (ranking invariant to unit change) for the mean etc.
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Thm 3 homogeneity requirement

title: Model Comparison and Calibration Assessment: User Guide for Consistent Scoring Functions in Machine Learning and Actuarial Practice
authors: T. Fissler, C. Lorentzen, M. Mayer
one_line_what_it_does: Poisson/Gamma/Tweedie deviance as consistent scores for the mean; homogeneous Bregman family appendix; scale and exposure discussion
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 / Thm 3 (Poisson deviance among Bregman losses, homogeneity)

title: Logs with zeros? Some problems and solutions
one_line_what_it_does: Proves any log-like transformation incl. log(1+Y) gives ATEs arbitrarily sensitive to units when extensive margin moves; recommends Poisson/PPML; Appx C discusses structural models Y=exp(a+D b)U
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 (unit/scale dependence of log1p response to a multiplicative shift; e(m) is the Poisson-specific closed form); Prop 2

title: Count (and Count-Like) Data in Finance
authors: J. B. Cohn, Z. Liu, M. I. Wardlaw
one_line_what_it_does: Shows log1plus regression coefficient differs from log-linear one by factor ~E[y|x]/(1+E[y|x]) and can have wrong sign; recommends Poisson (PPML); framing with multiplicative structure y=exp(xb)u
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 (first-order loading of a multiplicative shock on log1p scale increases with mean; e(m) vs m/(1+m))

title: Scale-Equivariant Transformations / When Are Estimates Independent of Measurement Units?
one_line_what_it_does: Only log and power transforms give unit-invariant t-stats, coefficients and semi-elasticities in OLS/GLM/Tobit
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1/2 (log1p non-invariance); Thm 3 flavour (characterisation by scale invariance)

title: Overcoming systematic errors caused by log-transformation of normalized single-cell RNA sequencing data
one_line_what_it_does: Size-factor-normalised counts then log(+pseudocount): mean of log depends on mean and variance of counts so a gene with no DE shows spurious log-scale differences between cells of different size factor; derives pseudo-count bound
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 (mean-dependent response of log-pseudocount scale to depth) and partial removal by normalisation

title: Comparison of transformations for single-cell RNA-seq data
one_line_what_it_does: Delta-method shifted log with size factors, pseudo-count = 1/(4 alpha) and overdispersion; size-factor division scales counts and violates common mean-variance relation; benchmark
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 / normalisation discussion

title: Feature selection and dimension reduction for single-cell RNA-Seq based on a multinomial model
authors: F. W. Townes, S. C. Hicks, M. J. Aryee, R. A. Irizarry
one_line_what_it_does: UMI counts ~ multinomial given totals; log-CPM with pseudocount distorts zeros vs nonzeros depending on size factor; deviance residuals / GLM-PCA
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 (conditional-on-total multinomial profiling); depth distortion on log scale

title: Normalization and variance stabilization of single-cell RNA-seq data using regularized negative binomial regression
one_line_what_it_does: Different gene groups cannot be normalised by one scaling factor; counts-depth relation is gene/mean dependent
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 (gene-dependent depth loading)

title: Normalization for sampled count data (formerly Depth normalization for single-cell genomics count data)
one_line_what_it_does: log1p after proportional fitting leaves depth structure; PFlog1pPF (shifted CLR) removes it
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 (partial removal of depth by library-size normalisation)

title: Pseudo maximum likelihood methods: applications to Poisson models
authors: C. Gourieroux, A. Monfort, A. Trognon
one_line_what_it_does: Poisson PML consistent for the mean-parameters under multiplicative error; basis of PPML
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 (Poisson deviance consistent under multiplicative nuisance)

title: Econometric Models for Count Data with an Application to the Patents-R&D Relationship
authors: J. Hausman, B. H. Hall, Z. Griliches
one_line_what_it_does: Poisson with multiplicative firm fixed effects; conditional on the within-firm total gives multinomial
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 (multinomial profiling of a multiplicative group nuisance)

title: Understanding the Multinomial-Poisson Transformation
authors: P. Guimaraes, O. Figueiredo, D. Woodward
one_line_what_it_does: Poisson with one dummy per group reproduces multinomial/conditional-logit estimates (Palmgren 1981; Baker 1994)
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 (profiling = conditioning on total)

title: Distributed Multinomial Regression
one_line_what_it_does: Poisson factorises into multinomial given total times Poisson total; ignoring the total is valid for inference on the shares
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 (scale-profiled deviance ranks shape only)

title: Practical Aspects of Implementing the Multinomial PML Estimator
one_line_what_it_does: Multinomial PML equals Poisson PML with full set of dummies
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2

title: Maximum likelihood estimation for multinomial-Poisson models: a generalization of Birch's numerical invariance results
authors: (author not captured; cited as Lang 1996 in another result)
one_line_what_it_does: Birch invariance: multinomial vs Poisson fitted values coincide under homogeneous constraints
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2

title: alpha-Divergence is unique, belonging to both f-divergence and Bregman divergence classes
one_line_what_it_does: KL (and alpha-divergences on positive measures) is the unique intersection of f-divergences and Bregman divergences
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Thm 3 flavour (uniqueness of KL/Poisson among Bregman under an invariance requirement)

title: The coefficient of determination R2 and intra-class correlation coefficient from GLMMs revisited and expanded
authors: S. Nakagawa, P. C. D. Johnson, H. Schielzeth
one_line_what_it_does: Observed-scale vs latent-scale variance decomposition (marginal/conditional R2, ICC) for Poisson/NB GLMMs via delta method, lognormal approx, trigamma
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 ceiling (share of between-group variance from random effect; delta-method distribution-specific variance)

title: The transformation of Poisson, binomial and negative-binomial data
one_line_what_it_does: Asymptotic expansions of mean/variance of sqrt and log(x+c) transforms of Poisson/NB counts
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 delta-method remainder (large-m expansion of E log(x+c))

title: Is H&E Image-to-Spatial Transcriptomics Simpler Than It Looks?
one_line_what_it_does: Exact decomposition of MSE into slide-level and within-slide components; MeanOnly baseline gets Pearson 0.69 / flat R2 0.43; full-text keyword scan found no mention of depth, library size, Poisson, log1p or ceiling
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Application setting (between-slide share), but no depth-loading theory

title: Translating histopathology foundation model embeddings (STpath)
one_line_what_it_does: Reports donor/individual batch effect clustering in foundation-model embeddings that confounds tile-level prediction
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Application setting

title: A Large-Scale Benchmark of Cross-Modal Learning for Histology and Gene Expression in Spatial Transcriptomics (HESCAPE)
one_line_what_it_does: Identifies batch effects as key factor degrading expression prediction in HEST-bench
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Application setting

title: Volatility prediction comparison via robust volatility proxies: an empirical deviation perspective
one_line_what_it_does: Reviews Patton robust/homogeneous losses and studies proxy deviation
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Finance analogue

title: Scaling and measurement error sensitivity of scoring rules for distribution forecasts
one_line_what_it_does: Extends Patton Prop 3 (homogeneity => rescaling invariance) to scoring rules for distribution forecasts
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 2 / finance analogue

title: Normalization of single-cell RNA-seq counts by log(x+1) or log(1+x)
one_line_what_it_does: Discusses log(x+1) vs log(1+x) normalisation order and what differences are preserved
bears_on_which_part_of_claim: Prop 1 context (normalisation/log order)
